The owner's 16:26Z update (relaying root 16:15) accidentally started a second instance of the step's agent; the original instance, running since about 15:55Z, saw the other's edits and reported it, and at 16:35Z the owner stopped the whole SM8 workflow. The owner reports the other instance committed nothing and did not touch the owner worktree after these edits began; a listing of every file in the session work area and /private/tmp/labsbx changed after 15:55Z shows no attempt directory, test log, ledger or temporary test tree other than this step's own; and the shared fixture-use log /private/tmp/labsbx/eb1c_sm_fixture_uses.jsonl, appended by every control that builds the compiled test double, has no entry between 15:55:28Z (the review's last) and 16:11:05Z, and its 40 entries from 16:11:05Z to 16:35:18Z are exactly chain1's (22 test processes: 17 two-test attempts, 4 one-test attempts, the interrupted one). One file in this step's own directory was written by the other instance: tmp/wt_now.diff (16:33:08Z, 3,986 B, sha256 f5a803d6e748260989b34f15a8a14ef00db91fbd8361755781fbb5870b76a6e4), a copy of the owner-worktree diff at that moment (not used here).

observation_for_root_not_changed: A held server whose process exits after the last health poll, once every call of the last pair was answered, is recorded only by the closing stop (server_stopped with return code 9) and never as server_down. This follows protocol 5.3's 5 s poll and the EB1c boundary check at IDLE, which the horizon path (DECIDED) does not visit; no episode is affected (every call was answered before the exit) and no process is started after it, so no serving-manifest check is owed. Production is unchanged; named so root can rule whether a closing stop that finds a crash return code should be a server_down.
